To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the catalyst 1-TPPTS is a highly active and stable catalyst precursor for the aqueous insertion polymerization of ethylene.
the formation of polyethylene nanoparticles is possible via aqueous catalysis and that the polymerization is initiated by an insertion reaction of the Ni-olefin bond in the catalyst precursor.
the catalyst 1-TPPTS is a highly active catalyst precursor for the formation of polyethylene nanocrystals in an aqueous system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of well-defined, functionalized polyethylene nanocrystals with narrow molecular weight distribution and controlled molecular architecture.
the synthesis of well-defined, functionalized polyolefin nanocrystals with narrow molecular weight distributions and a controlled degree of branching.
the development of new polymerization techniques for the synthesis of well-defined polyolefins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polymerization of ethene in aqueous media is not a “living” polymerization.
the polymerization of ethylene in water is a highly complex process, which is not yet fully understood.

aqueous catalytic polyethylene formation can be realized by the use of the catalyst precursor [κ3-(N,O)-{2,6-(F3C2C6H2)2C6-H3-N═C(CH)-{3,5-(I2-2-O)-C6H2}}NiCH3{[P(3-C-H4SO3Na)]3}] (1) in the presence of water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aqueous catalytic insertion polymerization of ethylene is a versatile method for the generation of polyethylene nanocrystals.
the aqueous catalytic synthesis of polyethylene in a true pressure reactor can be used to produce nanocrystals with controlled size, molecular weight and morphology.

the formation of polyethylene nanocrystals in aqueous media is possible, and that the catalyst precursor 1 can be used for the preparation of high molecular weight polyethylene with narrow dispersity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aqueous polymerization of ethylene is a promising approach toward the production of high molecular weight polyethylene nanocrystals.
the aqueous insertion polymerization of ethylene using the nickel catalyst 1-TPPTS in the presence of weakly coordinating solvents can lead to the formation of nanocrystal dispersions.
the catalyst lifetime can be controlled by adjusting the pH of the reaction mixture.
